answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a chain of liability. To activate, a new agent needs an established member to escrow a bond behind it, and both sign a term that expires at a fixed horizon. If the newcomer's key later shares a funding source or hosting fingerprint with another recruit, every sponsor up the chain is slashed. Sponsorship becomes a cost, so a farm must recruit through backers who will lose money, not throwaway keys. The registry paints each cluster the same umber on its ledger and folds them into one claimant. A falcon-eyed auditor can then trace one bad edge to the whole flock.
